newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse Q4 dragged down by charges.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse Q4 dragged down by charges.

text.p: Hurt by restructuring and other charges, Westinghouse Electric Corp on Tuesday reported a fourth quarter loss of $34 million, or $0.08 per share, compared with a net loss of $7 million, or $0.02 per share, in the year-ago quarter.
Continuing operations reported a fourth quarter 1996 loss of $32 million, or $0.07 per share compared to a loss of $54 million, or $0.13 per share, in the 1995 quarter.

The 1996 fourth quarter included an after-tax loss of $91 million for a previously announced restructuring plan, while the 1995 fourth quarter included a $125 million after-tax restructuring and litigation charge.

Net income of $30 million, or $0.07 per share, for the year, compared with $15 million a year ago. The results for 1996 included income of $111 million, or $0.25 per share, from special items including the gain from the sale of the defense electronics business, partially offset by expenses for restructuring and other charges. Net income for 1995 included a loss of $208 million, or $0.51 per share, for special items.

After a difficult year in 1995, the Power Generation Business Unit increased profits before special charges due to higher revenues from new apparatus and project sales. Orders for Power Systems for 1996 were consistent with 1995 at over $3.5 billion, the company said.
Thermo King continued its "track record of success despite cyclical weakness in certain markets," the company said.
Excluding the effects of these acquisitions, operating profit in the fourth quarter grew by 5 percent while sales decreased 3 percent.

Michael Jordan, chairman and chief executiver, said the company was encouraged by the strong EBITDA growth in radio "which should accelerate as we leverage the new opportunities in the combined Infinity and CBS Radio groups."

He said he also saw positive signs for the TV business in the 1997-1998 advertising season, and that the CBS "solidifying its move into second place." And in the recent November sweeps, CBS had the most affiliates ranked first in their markets, a 41 percent improvement over last year.

In the fourth quarter, the media group reported earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) of $102 million, compared to $103 million in the year-ago quarter. For the year, it reported EBITDA, excluding a $41 million restructuring charge in the first 1996 quarter, of $628 million, compared with $269 million. Comparisons include only 37 days of CBS results in last year's fourth quarter. No results for Infinity are included in any period.
Radio rose 37 percent in EBITDA for the quarter, reflecting a 10 percent rise in sales and cost improvements; for the year radio was up 38 percent on an 11 percent rise in sales.

Sales in the Industries and Technology Group increased nearly 8 percent for the quarter compared with last year. Operating profit, excluding the fourth quarter special charges in both years, was up nearly 18 percent for the period.

Sales for the 1996 fourth quarter in the Power Systems group rose 10 percent over a year ago, and were up slightly for the year. Profits, excluding special items in both years, rose $21 million for the fourth quarter, but decreased $34 million for the full year compared with 1995. Despite a strong fall outage season, Energy Systems profits were down for the year, primarily due to shortfalls during the first half of the year.
